- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above immediate prior high.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast values are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; adjust final 5–7 days upward if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment history shows rapid shift from negative to positive, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is underestimating; apply upward bias of 2–4% for next forecast.
